episodes.title: In India, This Cult Leader Promised Them Millions. He Gave Them a Nightmare | Full Documentary
episodes.description:
Catching a Scammer / This true crime series reveals the untold details of the cat-and-mouse game between investigators and the craftiest criminals – and we hear it from the very people themselves. Investigations in Taiwan, Singapore and Indonesia follow the hunt to bring these crooks to justice by police, prosecutors, and sometimes even ordinary concerned citizens in this three-part series. The first episode takes us to Taiwan - home to the some of the world’s most sophisticated phone scam syndicates. The second features the inside story of Singapore’s own Tinder Swindler, who made the news for posing as the ‘heir of a Korean billionaire’. Lastly, in Indonesia, the charismatic cult leader, who claimed the power to conjure money out of thin air, soon moved on from scams to murder, when cracks in his operations appeared. The show tells the twisted tales of the devastating losses caused by the most cold-hearted schemes of swindlers and scam rings across Asia.

00:00 - Introduction: The discovery of Abdul Gani's body.
01:02 - The Legend of Dimas Kanjeng: Taat Pribadi’s rise and his claims of supernatural powers.
01:56 - The Money Multiplication Trick: How he lured thousands into his "padepokan."
04:58 - The Victims' Stories: Entrepreneurs explain why they invested billions.
10:31 - The Disappearances: The fate of Dimas’s close associates, Abdul Gani and Ismail.
19:18 - Police Raid & Arrest: A massive operation to capture the "King."
22:09 - Exposing the Scam: The truth behind the fake money and psychological manipulation.
28:48 - Trial & Conviction: Legal proceedings for murder and fraud.
42:46 - The Aftermath: The current state of the sect and its remaining followers.

episodes.title: The Waco Siege or When a Cult Decides to End It All | Full Documentary
episodes.description:
"THE WACO SIEGE" / Spring 1993, the small town of Waco, Texas, is in the news: a religious group, the Branch Davidians, have been holed up in a ranch for weeks. The American police are convinced that the group is a cult led by David Koresh, a man with an outstanding arrest warrant. Worse still, the cult is said to possess over 150 weapons and 200,000 rounds of ammunition. Despite repeated negotiations, Koresh refused to surrender, and the "Davidians" remained entrenched in their residence. The authorities feared mass suicide, but they also knew that any intervention could result in a bloodbath. How did negotiations proceed during the 51-day siege? What really happened within the sect and among the authorities?
